title: Release Runlimit 0.3.0 to crates.io
description: Finalize, validate, publish, tag, and verify the coordinated Runlimit 0.3.0 workspace release.

title: Split GCRA-specific failures from MemoryStoreError
description: Implement the abstraction review finding: introduce an algorithm-specific GcraStoreError for GCRA admission failures, remove the GCRA-only ArithmeticOverflow variant from MemoryStoreError, preserve common bounded-storage failures, migrate public signatures/tests/docs/smoke coverage, and run the required workspace checks.
close_reason: Completed GcraStoreError API split, migrated tests/docs/smoke coverage, and passed required workspace checks

title: Implement validated whole-codebase simplifications
description:
Canonical implementation record for the validated whole-codebase simplification audit at repository HEAD 0763d6def1aad2e91b63616a3884da1ca0ac81e3.

Coverage contract: 25 explicit subsystem boundaries spanning runlimit-core policy, keying, decisions, limiter orchestration, observation, and errors; runlimit-memory configuration, fixed-window store, GCRA store, and shared shard machinery; runlimit-postgres public API, key/protocol derivation, fixed-window persistence, capacity sharding, cleanup, observation, and bundled migrations; HTTP contracts; Axum bridge; workspace/build infrastructure; release tooling; compatibility/tooling checks; documentation; and Beads/admin metadata. The audit inspected 74 tracked paths. Every row ended as either a retained recommendation or an explicit skip.

Retained work: nine recommendations are represented by child issues R-CORE-02-1, R-CORE-04-1, R-MEM-04-2, R-MEM-03-1, R-CORE-05-2, R-CORE-05-1, R-MEM-02-1, R-TEST-01-1, and R-TOOL-01-1.

Explicit completed skips: CORE-01 key derivation and opaque subjects already centralize the security protocol; CORE-03 batch validation already has a clear typed boundary; CORE-06 limiter orchestration is intentionally thin; MEM-01 configuration types already prevent invalid capacity/cleanup combinations; PG-01 public facade, PG-02 stable advisory-lock/key protocol, PG-03 fixed-window SQL flow, PG-04 capacity-shard protocol, PG-05 cleanup API, PG-06 PostgreSQL observation semantics, and PG-07 immutable migrations had no simplification above the materiality threshold; HTTP-01 framework-neutral contracts and AXUM-01 extraction/response mapping correctly leave policy at the application boundary; INFRA-01 workspace/build metadata is already small; TOOL-02 compatibility and smoke checks encode useful public/wire ownership; DOC-01 documentation duplication is intentional audience-specific guidance; ADMIN-01 Beads and contributor metadata is operational infrastructure, not product-state complexity.

Cross-cutting conclusions: preserve distinct backend semantics instead of forcing a common storage abstraction; use closed state representations only where invalid states or unreachable branches exist; keep hot-path allocation changes behind measurement; treat public Rust API cuts as one semver-signaled migration; do not alter immutable migrations, fixed-window/GCRA semantics, policy fingerprints, PostgreSQL time authority, advisory-lock or capacity-shard derivation, all-or-nothing ordering, fail-closed capacity behavior, or quota-consumption guarantees.

Deduplication and supersession: the two memory routing findings have separate ownership, with GCRA evaluation-state cleanup preceding shared batch topology extraction; observation construction and decision views remain separate but sequence decision views first; no recommendation merely moves branching behind a new type. All weaker style-only, speculative, or protocol-risk proposals were rejected.

Priority order: (1) core duration validation error, (2) decision read views, (3) GCRA evaluation state, (4) single-check shard effects subject to benchmark, (5) cleanup observation state, (6) admission observation factories, (7) shared batch topology, (8) isolated PostgreSQL schema fixture, (9) obsolete release preflight removal.

Audit log: repository inventory and call-site/test mapping completed; bounded subsystem reviews completed; coordinator independently verified retained evidence; coverage, duplication/ownership, materiality/over-abstraction, schema completeness, and dependency-aware ranking passes completed; repository was clean at audit handoff. This epic stores implementation work only; the audit itself made no source changes and ran no tests.
acceptance_criteria: All nine child findings are either implemented and closed or explicitly rejected with repository evidence; public API removals are documented as a semver-signaled migration; affected work passes cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, and the disposable PostgreSQL suite where relevant; no immutable migration or persistent cross-replica protocol is changed in place.
close_reason: Completed: all nine validated simplification findings are implemented and closed; the semver-signaled public API removal is documented; required fmt, clippy, workspace, mocked release, and disposable PostgreSQL validations pass; immutable migrations and persistent protocols remain unchanged.

title: Replace partial public policy-error conversion
description:
Audit finding R-CORE-02-1. Authoritative subsystem: runlimit-core policy configuration and validation.

Evidence: crates/runlimit-core/src/policy.rs lines 323-340 use a shared duration validator that returns a public PolicyError; the GCRA mapping around lines 384 onward converts it; the public From conversion around lines 680-692 has panic arms for valid public ZeroLimit and LimitTooLarge variants.

Current complexity: an internal partial conversion is exposed as a total public trait implementation, so callers can construct inputs that reach unreachable panic branches. The representation hides the real three-way duration-validation outcome.

Target: introduce a private closed duration-validation error with zero, fractional-millisecond, and too-large cases; map it exhaustively to each public policy error; remove the partial public From implementation. Keep the change local and do not redesign policy configuration.

Smallest scope: crates/runlimit-core/src/policy.rs and directly affected core tests/public migration notes. Preserve validation precedence, exact documented error semantics, serde behavior, and storage fingerprints.

Risks: deliberate public Rust source break from removing From; subtle error-precedence drift when multiple inputs are invalid; accidental fingerprint or serde changes.

Validation: characterize all duration mappings for both fixed-window and GCRA policies, including GCRA zero and too-large cases and multi-invalid precedence; retain fingerprint and serde compatibility assertions. Confidence: high. Impact: medium. Effort: small. Blast radius: core public API.
acceptance_criteria: No public conversion can panic for a constructible PolicyError; duration validation is represented by a private exhaustive type; existing validation precedence, messages/semantics, serde, and fingerprints remain unchanged; migration notes and focused tests cover the removed public conversion.
close_reason: Implemented private exhaustive duration validation, removed the partial public conversion, documented the API cut, and added focused mapping/precedence tests.

title: Expose discriminated decision read views
description:
Audit finding R-CORE-04-1. Authoritative subsystem: runlimit-core structured decisions.

Evidence: crates/runlimit-core/src/decision.rs exposes decisions through multiple optional accessors whose valid combinations depend on the internal variant; observation and HTTP callers repeat those shape assumptions, including crates/runlimit-core/src/observation.rs and crates/runlimit-http/src/lib.rs. README examples and compatibility smoke crates are major public call sites.

Current complexity: callers reconstruct a discriminated state from nullable accessors, permitting contradictory downstream handling and repeated variant branching.

Target: add read-only DecisionView and BatchDecisionView discriminated views. DecisionView should distinguish Allowed with inline payload, Denied, and quota-only ShadowDenied. BatchDecisionView should distinguish an allowed decision slice from denial index plus payload. Keep existing accessors and serialization initially.

Smallest scope: crates/runlimit-core/src/decision.rs, the core facade re-export, direct observation/HTTP consumers where the view materially removes reconstruction, README examples, compatibility smoke crates, and focused tests.

Risks: accidentally changing wire representation, losing the input-index contract for batch denials, or creating a second mutable decision model. Views must borrow existing decisions and remain additive for the first slice.

Validation: prove view-to-variant and legacy-accessor parity for all variants; retain serde/wire tests; compile public API smoke crates and exercise HTTP mapping. Confidence: high. Impact: medium. Effort: medium. Blast radius: additive public API and selected consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Borrowed discriminated views cover every decision and batch-decision variant without nullable-state reconstruction; old accessors and serialized forms remain behaviorally identical for the additive slice; denial indices and ordering remain exact; core, HTTP, README, and smoke-call-site validation is updated.
close_reason: Added exhaustive borrowed decision views, re-exported them publicly, migrated observation/HTTP/README/smoke consumers, and preserved legacy accessors and Serde wire forms.

title: Make post-preflight GCRA arithmetic failure unrepresentable
description:
Audit finding R-MEM-04-2. Authoritative subsystem: runlimit-memory GCRA store.

Evidence: crates/runlimit-memory/src/gcra.rs uses one EvaluationError representation for both quota denial and arithmetic overflow, then carries branches that later phases treat as unreachable after preflight.

Current complexity: quota outcomes and impossible-after-preflight failures share one error channel. Later code must defend against states the control flow says cannot occur, obscuring the important rule that a later arithmetic overflow supersedes an earlier denial and prevents mutation.

Target: represent quota evaluation as QuotaEvaluation with Allowed(PendingAllowance) and Denied(QuotaDenial); reserve an outer Result only for ArithmeticOverflow. Use the types to encode which states are legal after preflight.

Smallest scope: crates/runlimit-memory/src/gcra.rs and its focused tests. Do not change public GcraStore interfaces or create a cross-backend abstraction.

Risks: changing overflow-versus-denial precedence, cleanup timing, quota consumption, batch atomicity, or observer effects. A failed arithmetic operation must still perform no cleanup or storage mutation.

Validation: characterize single and batch allowed/denied paths, later-overflow superseding earlier denial, zero mutation and cleanup on overflow, input-order decisions, and observer behavior. Confidence: high. Impact: medium. Effort: small. Blast radius: local state/control flow.
acceptance_criteria: Post-preflight types contain no unreachable quota/arithmetic combinations; later arithmetic overflow still supersedes earlier denial; overflow causes no cleanup or mutation; GCRA single/batch semantics, all-or-nothing behavior, ordering, and observation remain unchanged.
close_reason: Separated quota outcomes from arithmetic failure with QuotaEvaluation and ArithmeticOverflow, removed unreachable post-preflight branches, and added later-overflow atomicity/observation coverage.

title: Represent single-check shard effects directly
description:
Audit finding R-MEM-03-1. Authoritative subsystem: runlimit-memory single-check result/effect ownership across fixed-window and GCRA stores.

Evidence: crates/runlimit-memory/src/store.rs and crates/runlimit-memory/src/gcra.rs package every operationally successful single check as a one-element effect Vec before observer delivery, including paths with no configured observer.

Current complexity: the result model uses a batch collection for an intrinsically single effect, creating avoidable allocation/collection mechanics and making single-versus-batch ownership less explicit.

Target: use a local Evaluation<T, E> form whose single-check path carries one ShardEffect directly while the batch path carries Vec<ShardEffect>. Keep observer delivery order and lock-release behavior unchanged.

Smallest scope: the two memory store implementation files plus observer tests and a narrowly scoped allocation/benchmark check. Do not introduce public generic machinery or a shared executor.

Risks: hot-path refactoring may not produce measurable value, can accidentally deliver observations under a lock, and can change effect order. This recommendation is gated: reject or demote it if measurement shows no credible allocation or clarity gain.

Validation: add missing GCRA observer parity tests, prove callbacks occur after unlocking in the same order, compare allocation/hot-path behavior, and run all memory semantics tests. Confidence: high. Impact: medium. Effort: small. Blast radius: two backend internals.
acceptance_criteria: Single checks no longer require a one-element effect collection; batch effects remain ordered; observers run after locks are released with unchanged payloads; focused measurement demonstrates a credible benefit, otherwise the issue is closed as rejected with evidence.
close_reason: Completed: direct single-check effects remove one allocation per check in both memory backends; 100k-check release allocation comparison measured 100k to 0, with observer ordering/unlock parity covered.

title: Close cleanup observation effect state
description:
Audit finding R-CORE-05-2. Authoritative subsystem: runlimit-core cleanup observation contracts.

Evidence: crates/runlimit-core/src/observation.rs represents cleanup results as Option<u64> combined with ConsumptionStatus and exposes construction that permits nonsensical combinations.

Current complexity: independent nullable count and effect-status fields encode one lifecycle outcome but permit contradictory states such as a confirmed removal count paired with an unknown outcome.

Target: use a private closed state with Confirmed(u64), DefinitelyNoEffect, and OutcomeUnknown, exposed through semantic factories and stable getters. Remove or restrict the raw constructor in the planned semver cut.

Smallest scope: crates/runlimit-core/src/observation.rs, backend construction call sites, public smoke/migration documentation, and observation tests. Keep backend-specific outcome semantics.

Risks: public Rust source break, Debug-output changes, and incorrectly collapsing unknown with definitely-no-effect.

Validation: exhaustively map every backend cleanup success/failure path to one closed state; assert getters and debug/serde promises actually documented; compile smoke consumers. Confidence: high. Impact: medium. Effort: small to medium. Blast radius: public observation construction.
acceptance_criteria: Cleanup observations cannot represent a confirmed count with a contradictory effect status; semantic factories preserve confirmed, definitely-no-effect, and unknown distinctions; all backend call sites are exhaustively mapped; the public cut is documented and validated.
close_reason: Completed: cleanup observations now use closed confirmed/no-effect/unknown states with semantic factories, stable getters/debug shape, exhaustive backend mapping tests, changelog migration notes, and external-consumer compilation.

title: Add semantic admission observation factories
description:
Audit finding R-CORE-05-1. Authoritative subsystem: runlimit-core admission observation construction.

Evidence: crates/runlimit-core/src/observation.rs exposes a raw seven-field admission-observation constructor; memory and PostgreSQL backends must repeatedly supply coupled policy metadata and failure fields. PostgreSQL intentionally reports one-item failed-batch metadata in a case where memory reports none.

Current complexity: raw positional construction permits metadata combinations that do not correspond to semantic events and spreads construction policy across backends.

Target: replace or restrict the raw constructor with semantic success/failure factories, pair policy identifier with its configuration fingerprint, and require the full ConsumptionStatus on failures. Preserve intentional backend-specific metadata differences; do not introduce a larger observation state machine.

Smallest scope: crates/runlimit-core/src/observation.rs and the memory/PostgreSQL call sites and tests that construct admission observations; public migration notes for a semver-signaled cut.

Risks: accidentally normalizing meaningful backend differences, changing event/debug shapes, or losing data on failed batches.

Validation: enumerate every fixed-window and GCRA single/batch success/failure factory call, preserve the PostgreSQL one-item failed-batch case and memory counterpart, and compile public smoke consumers. Confidence: high. Impact: low to medium. Effort: small to medium. Blast radius: public factories and backend call sites.
acceptance_criteria: Admission observations are created through semantic factories with coupled policy metadata; failure creation requires complete consumption status; intentional memory/PostgreSQL metadata differences remain characterized; raw invalid construction is removed or made private in a documented semver cut.
close_reason: Completed: raw admission construction is removed; policy ID/scope are internally coupled and derived from checks; semantic failure factories require full consumption status; memory and PostgreSQL metadata differences are characterized; changelog and external smoke are updated.

title: Centralize validated pre-lock batch routing
description:
Audit finding R-MEM-02-1. Authoritative subsystem: runlimit-memory shared shard routing machinery.

Evidence: crates/runlimit-memory/src/store.rs and crates/runlimit-memory/src/gcra.rs independently repeat the pre-lock batch mechanics for resolving per-input shard positions, sorting and deduplicating shard indices, counting feasibility, and acquiring locks in a stable order; crates/runlimit-memory/src/shards.rs owns the shared shard primitives.

Current complexity: duplicated routing assumptions make lock order, capacity preflight, and input-position recovery harder to compare across the two algorithms.

Target: add a private BatchTopology kernel in shards.rs containing sorted unique shard indices, resolved per-input positions, and per-shard counts/feasibility. Both stores consume it after policy/input validation and before locking.

Smallest scope: crates/runlimit-memory/src/shards.rs plus the relevant batch paths in store.rs and gcra.rs and characterization tests. Do not add public traits, a generic batch executor, or another per-input allocation.

Risks: changing exact error precedence, lock ordering, capacity behavior, duplicate-subject semantics, or algorithm-specific evaluation sequencing.

Validation: characterize validate then empty then per-shard-capacity then lock precedence; duplicate keys; mixed shards; full capacity; stable input-order decisions; deadlock-safe sorted lock order; and both algorithms' atomic no-mutation failures. Confidence: medium-high. Impact: medium. Effort: medium. Blast radius: shared memory batch routing.
acceptance_criteria: Both memory batch implementations consume one private validated topology representation; validation/error precedence, lock order, duplicate handling, capacity checks, input ordering, and all-or-nothing behavior remain unchanged; no public or over-generic executor abstraction is introduced.
close_reason: Completed: both memory batch paths now use one private BatchTopology for sorted routes, per-input positions, per-shard counts, structural capacity preflight, and lock order; focused precedence, routing, GCRA atomicity, and memory tests pass.

title: Introduce an explicit isolated PostgreSQL schema fixture
description:
Audit finding R-TEST-01-1. Authoritative subsystem: PostgreSQL integration-test infrastructure.

Evidence: crates/runlimit-postgres/tests/postgres.rs repeats schema naming, admin and primary pool ownership, search_path setup, additional-pool registration, migration setup, and teardown across 15 fixture callers, with mode booleans and lifecycle assumptions spread through helpers.

Current complexity: one fixture carries several optional resources and mode-dependent cleanup paths, making ownership and teardown order implicit.

Target: introduce a test-only IsolatedSchema fixture with named admin/primary/schema fields, two explicit factories for the established modes, a schema-bound pool builder, registration only for extra multi-pool resources, and explicit async teardown. Avoid Drop-based async cleanup and mode booleans.

Smallest scope: crates/runlimit-postgres/tests/postgres.rs. Do not modify bundled or host migrations.

Risks: leaking schemas/connections, closing pools in the wrong order, changing the default-schema migration side effect, or changing isolated create/cardinality and fillfactor assumptions.

Validation: migrate all 15 callers; assert search_path and close ordering; retain default-schema and isolated-schema behavior; run the ignored disposable PostgreSQL integration suite serially under default and all relevant feature sets. Confidence: high. Impact: medium in tests. Effort: medium. Blast radius: integration-test harness only.
acceptance_criteria: All existing PostgreSQL fixture callers use explicit lifecycle-owning schema fixtures without mode booleans; pool/schema teardown is deterministic and async; migration side effects, search_path, fillfactor, and cardinality behaviors remain unchanged; the required disposable PostgreSQL suites pass.
close_reason: Completed: all 15 isolated PostgreSQL callers now use an explicit lifecycle-owning IsolatedSchema with separate migration and cleanup factories, one schema-bound pool builder, registered extra pools only for multi-pool tests, asserted search_path and close ordering, and deterministic async teardown; default and all-feature disposable PostgreSQL suites pass 28/28.

title: Remove unreachable 0.2.0 name-reservation preflight
description:
Audit finding R-TOOL-01-1. Authoritative subsystem: release preparation and publication scripts.

Evidence: scripts/prepare-release.sh and scripts/publish-release.sh retain first-publication name-reservation branches specific to version 0.2.0, while current manifests are 0.3.x and the scripts verify manifest/tag version alignment before reaching those branches. The historical v0.2 tag preserves the original release procedure.

Current complexity: unreachable historical branching remains in the live release path and suggests a supported state that current version guards make impossible.

Target: remove only the 0.2.0 name-reservation arrays, helpers, and calls from the two scripts.

Smallest scope: scripts/prepare-release.sh and scripts/publish-release.sh. Preserve registry collision checks, checksum/provenance generation, dry-run behavior, and resumable publish behavior.

Risks: accidentally removing a still-live collision or resume guard adjacent to the historical code.

Validation: run bash syntax checks and a mocked/dry-run release flow covering current manifest validation, collision handling, provenance/checksum, and resume behavior. Confidence: high. Impact: low. Effort: trivial. Blast radius: release tooling.
acceptance_criteria: Only unreachable 0.2.0 name-reservation logic is removed; current version validation, registry collision detection, provenance/checksum generation, dry-run, and resume behavior remain covered and unchanged; both scripts pass bash syntax validation.
close_reason: Completed: removed only the unreachable 0.2.0 first-publication name-reservation arrays, helpers, and calls from both release scripts. Bash syntax, diff checks, mocked manifest/collision/fresh dry-run/provenance/checksum/resume flows, and full workspace fmt/clippy/tests pass.
